text.ShobobgroRugdush: Drad's a fancy pants who lives in a pretty house with a pretty wife because he screws over folks like you and me. He makes us puke.

text.LordDrad: The source of my income, of course. I bought it for a song from a foolish Orc. My ogres mine the gold, and I reap the reward.

text.LadyDrad: He works them in Bleak Mine. It's terrible. The guards beat the creatures mercilessly. That's all I can tell you. Now please, go.
I can't tell you about that. Please, just go.

text.LordDrad: Can you think of a better use for the mindless beasts? Under my eye, they do some good in this world.

text.ShobobgroRugdush: Lord Malacath doesn't want the little brothers locked up, working like donkeys so men don't get their pretty pink hands all dirty. Makes Him mad.
Malacath likes Orcs... when He likes anything. So you can approach the shrine. He won't hurt you. Really. Go ahead.
You're not one of Malacath's favorite people. He likes Orcs. Too bad for you.  So you approach His shrine at your own risk.
I guess you haven't heard. We don't like the 'beautiful people'. But maybe you can persuade me you're ugly inside...

text.AymarDouar: Then perhaps you should go, lest Vaermina take interest in your dreams.
To speak with Vaermina, you must offer a black soul gem to the Daedra Lord.
Here we worship Vaermina, praying for her to grant us true visions. What is your business here?

text.BasilErnarde: Meridia has spoken to you, and for that, you are blessed.
The spark of life is within you, and you are welcome here at Meridia's shrine. It is possible she will speak to you, under certain conditions.
Leave an offering at this shrine. Meridia demands tribute in the form of the remains of her enemies, the undead.

text.MelsMaryon: Then be on your way, lest you anger the Lady.
If you wish to speak to the Lady, visit her shrine at dawn or dusk.
Leave her an offering of glow dust, and perhaps she will deign to speak with you.

text.SE08DarkSeducerGrakendoUdico: Very well, Your Grace.

text.SE08GoldenSaintAurigDesha: Very well, Your Grace.

text.Jauffre: Nowhere is truly safe against the power arrayed against us. But we must play for time, at least...
Cloud Ruler Temple, I think. The hidden fortress of the Blades, in the mountains near Bruma. A few men can hold it against an army.
We should leave at once.
So it has not all gone against us. Thank Talos for that! We gained Uriel's heir, and lost the Amulet of Kings.
Martin cannot stay here. We have driven them off, but they will be back once they learn of Martin's survival. Which they will.
I should have known they could find it. Little can remain hid from a Daedra Lord. I underestimated the enemy. It will not happen again.
What of your mission to Kvatch?
We'll go together. But I fear the worst.

text.Eronor: I don't know. In the Chapel praying, I think. You must help us!
I don't know! I think they're right behind me! Prior Maborel is dead!
I was in the sheepfold when they attacked. I heard the Prior talking to someone.
Looked around the corner to see who it was. They looked like travellers, ordinary.
Suddenly weapons appeared in their hands and they cut the Prior down before he could move! They saw me watching and I ran.

text.MorGraGamorn: Then leave, and forget you have ever seen this place.
Perhaps you have been summoned. Perhaps Nocturnal desires your service, and has guided you here. Approach.

text.WeebumNa: I am Weebam-Na. What do you want?

text.Generic Imperial Male: He's always got some scam going with Bejeen, his partner. You might find them both at Weebum-Na's house.
She wasn't a bad sort until she hooked up with that rascal Weebam-Na. That's where you're likely to find her... at Weebam-Na's house.

text.Bejeen: Why... why would you ask? I've never heard of it. No idea what you're talking about. And Weebam-Na doesn't know, either.

text.WeebumNa: Never heard of the thing. And neither has Bejeen. You ask too many questions.

text.Generic Imperial Male: Eye of Nocturnal? Doesn't sound familiar to me.

text.MorGraGamorn: You have been given a task. Do it.
Approach the shrine, if you dare.
You should not be in this place. What is your business here? Do you believe yourself worthy to speak to Nocturnal?

text.Martin: The Emperor... that's an idea that will take some getting used to.
In any case, we need the Amulet first. Maybe Jauffre will know where to start.
Of course. The Amulet of Kings. So we... I... can take it to the Temple of the One and light the Dragonfires. And stop the Oblivion invasion.

text.MQ06MythicDawnDoorkeeper: Welcome, brother. The hour is late, but the Master still has need for willing hands.
You may pass into the Shrine. Harrow will take you to the Master for your initiation into the service of Lord Dagon.
Do not tarry. The time of Preparation is almost over. The time of Cleansing is near.
Welcome, sister. The hour is late, but the Master still has need for willing hands.
You may pass into the Shrine. Harrow will take you to the Master for your initiation into the service of Lord Dagon.
Do not tarry. The time of Preparation is almost over. The time of Cleansing is near.

text.Harrow: Then you have come here to die.
What? I must warn you, no one leaves this place who does not bind himself to the service of Lord Dagon.
But I am sure you will reconsider. You have proven yourself worthy and dedicated to have come this far.
I ask you one last time: give me your possessions. The Master requires it of all initiates.
Very good. Follow me. I will take you to the Shrine.

text.SEArctus: Blasphemy! Never utter the name of the Dark Deceiver lightly!
Though his body is beyond Oblivion, his soul encircles us... always watching, waiting to pounce with lethal aplomb.
He is the bringer of pain and pleasure; the blade that cuts through our sins like a scythe through wheat.
Only a true Demented can appreciate what it means to render his name.

text.SEDervenin: Yes, Arden-Sul. Doesn't the name simply roll wonderfully off the tongue?
He was the sovereign of thought and a regnant artist. To call him a simple craftsman would not suffice; know him as the Artificer Superior.
Words dripped like honey from his tongue and his songs were intoned with extraordinary verisimilitude.
Had we been blessed with his constant presence, the Isles would be a Maniac's paradise.

text.SECutter: Think of me fondly when you bury this axe deep into your foe's skull.
When you hack off an arm, the blood spurts out in surges.

text.SEDumagGraBonk: Mama used to say, "If sweet-talking doesn't work, try hitting him with a big stick!"
"Smacking an idiot in the head a few times is the surest way to win an argument," my Mama used to say.

text.SECutter: When you are really angry, it feels good to hack into someone with a giant blade.
With enough force, this will cleave through meat and bone.

text.SEDumagGraBonk: As you wish.

text.SECutter: Maybe later.

text.UrsanneLoche: Aleron never mentioned it to me before.

text.AleronLoche: Clever ruse. I wonder how many have died falling for it?
You haven't guessed it yet? There never was any Axe of Dragol. It was just a ruse to lure you out here.
I fell for the same trick. In my case, he told me if I retrieved the axe, he'd erase my debts. I was such an idiot to believe him.
You're now the prey in Kurdan's insane hunt, just like I am. And here, we'll most likely die.

text.KurdangroDragol: Yeah. It's a battleaxe with the word "Dragol" carved into the haft. Huge. You can't miss it. I ain't gonna draw you a picture.
Fine. But you better not take too long. I want that axe, and I want it now.
Fine. I have it waitin' for you at the dock next to the magic shop. Now get outta my sight.
Then Aleron may not be coming home from his... ahhh, journey, for a very long time. Like permanently.
Whenever yer ready, and it better be soon, I'll have a boat waitin' for you to get to Fort Grief Island.
I just learned that a family heirloom, the Axe of Dragol, which one of my stupid relatives lost, is located on Fort Grief Island in Niben Bay.
My informant tells me it's hidden in the main keep at the center. Dunno what's guardin' it, but I'm sure you can handle it.
If you go there and bring it back to me, I'll tell you exactly where Aleron is.

text.UrsanneLoche: You... you will? Oh thank you! Please be careful, I don't wish any harm to befall you either.
Yesterday, the usurer, Kurdan gro-Dragol, sent for my husband to meet him at the Lonely Suitor Lodge. He hasn't returned since.
I fear for his life. Kurdan isn't known for his patience. Please, I'm not wealthy, but I'd give anything to see Aleron again.
I knew it! I just knew he's gotten himself in hot water again. Please hurry and get him from that island.
I do miss him so. And when he gets back, I'm gonna kill him for making me worry like this!
It all started when Aleron became foolish, and started gambling. He'd visit the arena every week and spend our hard earned money on bets.
I told him to stop, but he didn't listen. He was certain he could win us a fortune and move us somewhere nicer, like the Imperial City.
It didn't take long for Aleron to begin losing. He resorted to borrowing money from a usurer to cover his losses and place new bets.
As you can imagine, it didn't pay off. He ended up owing around 500 gold. We could never have that kind of money to pay back the usurer.

text.Generic Breton Male: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic Breton Female: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic DarkElf Male: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic DarkElf Female: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic HighElf Male: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic HighElf Female: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic Imperial Male: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic Imperial Female: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic Khajiit Male: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.Generic Khajiit Female: Yeah, Ursanne's husband, Aleron is missing. Poor thing, I've seen her crying at the chapel. I hope someone can help her.

text.KurdangroDragol: Time's wastin'. He's safe... for now.
Maybe I know him, maybe I don't. But since yer so interested, I know somethin' that could jar my memory.
None of yer damn business. I'd tell you if I liked you... and I don't.

text.Harrow: So sayeth Lord Dagon. Praise be.
We have a new Sister who wishes to bind herself to the service of Lord Dagon.
We have a new Brother who wishes to bind himself to the service of Lord Dagon.

text.MankarCamoran: The Dragon Throne is empty, and we hold the Amulet of Kings!
Praise be to your Brothers and Sisters! Great shall be their reward in Paradise!

text.Ruma: Praise be!

text.MankarCamoran: Hear now the words of Lord Dagon.
"When I walk the earth again, the Faithful among you shall receive your reward: to be set above all other Mortals forever."
"As for the rest: the weak shall be winnowed; the timid shall be cast down; the mighty shall tremble at my feet and pray for pardon."

text.Ruma: So sayeth Lord Dagon. Praise be.

text.MankarCamoran: Your reward, Brothers and Sisters! The time of Cleansing draws nigh. I go now to Paradise. I shall return with Lord Dagon at the coming of the Dawn!

text.Ruma: Advance, initiate.

text.Generic Imperial Female: Praise be!

text.Generic Imperial Male: Praise be!

text.Generic Imperial Female: So sayeth Lord Dagon. Praise be.

text.Generic Imperial Male: So sayeth Lord Dagon. Praise be.

text.Ruma: She dares to touch the sacred Xarxes! Kill her!
He dares to touch the sacred Xarxes! Kill him!

text.GrayFox: I have written it down for you in this book. I've chosen you because you are the best. Good luck.
I arranged for the notable Celia Camoran to want to read a particular Elder Scroll. Don't ask how. However, she will be... unavoidably detained.
You will take her place. Do not speak to the priests. They are blindfolded and will not realize it isn't her unless you speak.
As the guildmaster, I am waiving bloodprice for anyone you kill during this heist. However, I can't stop the Watch from putting a price on your head.
Once you are inside the palace itself, you need to find the reading room. The blind priests will deliver a scroll to you there.
My scrying with Savilla's Stone has provided clues, but not the details. I know the tools you will need there, but not the obstacles themselves.
The boots of Springheel Jak will allow you to leap to an unreachable place. They will also protect you from a long fall.
The Arrow of Extrication is the only way to unlock the final door. Take them both.
In the Imperial Sewers. Here is the key for the gate to that section of the sewers. I picked the pocket of Ocato himself to get it.
The Elder Scrolls are kept in the Imperial Palace behind a door that cannot be breached.  Savilla's Stone has revealed a path around this door.
You will have to travel the Old Way. Once used as an escape route for Imperial Emperors, it has been forgotten for centuries.
To unseal the entrance you must sneak into the basement of the palace and activate the Glass of Time, whatever that is.
I understand. I don't want anyone taking on this job unless they feel up to it. Return to me when you are more confident.
Capital! I have worked for eleven years planning this heist. Savilla's Stone provided the last bit of information I needed.

text.Amusei: The Gray Fox requests a meeting. Please travel to Othrelo's house in the Imperial City Elven Gardens.

text.Agata: She is not well. I hope her amulet can be found soon.
Her condition remains unchanged. I appreciate you inquiring about her.

text.RightWind: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?
You get used to the cold. Got a good set of fur boots to keep my feet warm. Give a Nord a good thumping to keep the blood flowing, khah-khah-khah.
We are from Bruma.

text.Generic Breton Female: The Countess sent Captain Burd to deal with that Oblivion Gate outside of town. We're all praying that they'll be all right.

text.Generic Breton Male: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?

text.YvaraChannitte: Captain Burd and I make a good pair. He understands Nords and the North, while I appreciate the subtleties of southern culture and politics.

text.GanLuseph: This is my first posting after Arcane University. The Countess and Burd like my work well enough.

text.JeanneFrasoric: You know what it's like. Make lots of friends, and look busy. Same as anywhere.

text.Generic Breton Male: We are from Bruma.

text.Generic Breton Female: We are from Bruma.

text.AlvalUvani: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?
We are from Bruma.

text.Karinnarre: The Countess sent Captain Burd to deal with that Oblivion Gate outside of town. We're all praying that they'll be all right.

text.Generic HighElf Male: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?

text.Suurootan: No need to go to the Imperial City. Bruma may look like a Skyrim town, but we've got all the comforts of the warm Nibenean south.

text.Volanaro: It's a little too rugged up here for me. Add a couple hairs to a Nord and you've got a bear.

text.Generic HighElf Male: We are from Bruma.

text.Karinnarre: We are from Bruma.

text.NarinaCarvain: Captain Burd wanted to attack the Oblivion Gate immediately, but I ordered him to wait for you.
But you must hurry! I'm afraid of what might happen if the daedra are able to get a foothold here.

text.Generic Imperial Male: The Captain said you've been inside one of those Oblivion Gate things. Said you knew how to destroy them. I sure hope you can help us.

text.Generic Imperial Female: The Countess sent Captain Burd to deal with that Oblivion Gate outside of town. We're all praying that they'll be all right.

text.Generic Imperial Male: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?

text.HumilisNonius: I'm new here in Bruma myself. I'm from down Heartland way. Nords up here... no offense... don't work as hard as us Imperial Heartlanders.

text.IsaRaman: We're trying to bring the comfort of the Chapel to the Nords here, but Bruma's Nords stick to their heathen gods and uncivilized practices.

text.ArentusFalvius: I'm here to show Bruma's errant Nords the path to the true faith. They must put aside their heathen gods and worship the Nine.

text.NarinaCarvain: Some see only the conflicts between northern and southern cultures, but I see the way they are stronger when woven together.

text.GerichSenarel: As Captain Burd says, we have to stay on the good side of the local Nords. It ain't their fault they're ignorant barbarians.

text.SelenaOrania: Well, sometimes I feel we're not welcome here. The Nords don't like Heartlanders very much.

text.JantusBrolus: Istirus and I used to be adventurers, but we've retired here. Bruma is far from civilization, but we're ready for a little peace and quiet.

text.ArnoraAuria: I can't help myself. I'm just a sucker for well-heeled men. That Olav, for example, at the Tap and Tack. He's dreamy. And successful, too.

text.HelviusCecia: All I need is a roof, some bread, and blessings of the Nine. Bruma is Gods' country, and the Gods are good to me.

text.BrotchCalus: I'm retired from public practice. I only take students in Alchemy to support my hobbies.

text.Generic Imperial Male: We are from Bruma.

text.Generic Imperial Female: We are from Bruma.

text.Jskar: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?
We are from Bruma.

text.Generic Nord Female: The Countess sent Captain Burd to deal with that Oblivion Gate outside of town. We're all praying that they'll be all right.

text.Generic Nord Male: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?

text.Petrine: Sorry. All I have is paints. Serviceable beasts, but nothing special. We Nords are no great fanciers of horse flesh, except in stews, I'm afraid.

text.Olav: The Countess is Heartland Nibenean, and so are most guildsmen and chapelmen, but most others are as Nordish as you'll find.

text.HafidHollowleg: Lyra Rosentia collects Akaviri artifacts. She might have a project in mind. Her house is west of the chapel.

text.Logvaar: Nords who drink either get friendly or mean. I'm here to deal with the mean ones.

text.SnartheCook: We're still in Cyrodiil here in Bruma, but just barely. We build for the cold, just like in Skyrim.

text.Skjorta: We drink because we're happy. We're Nords. It's just the thick tongue and fat head the day after that makes me unhappy.

text.Olfand: Just like Skyrim, except for all the tight-ass Heartlanders around. All work and chapel... no wonder they're so sour.

text.Fjotreid: I work hard. Folks like Skjorta and Olfand give us Nords a bad name, drinking and carrying on until all hours.

text.Burd: I make sure my guards treat the local Nords and their ways with respect.

text.Honmund: Plenty of mineral desposits in the Jerall Mountains. I'm out for weeks at a time by myself, but I don't mind it.

text.Alga: Bruma's a funny place... half Cyrodiil and half Skyrim. I'm old Nord all the way. I keep the old songs and stories alive.

text.OngartheWorldWeary: Bruma is a perfect town for a Nord man of leisure. Bracing mountain air, good food and drink, and lively Nord fellowship.

text.Regner: I hate it here. Came here with Edla. All these snooty Southerners. And damn guards won't let anyone have any fun.

text.EdlaDarkHeart: One place is pretty much like another. Regner hates it, but Regner hates everything.

text.Generic Nord Male: We are from Bruma.

text.Generic Nord Female: We are from Bruma.

text.BumphgraGash: The Countess sent Captain Burd to deal with that Oblivion Gate outside of town. We're all praying that they'll be all right.
Yeah, you think Bruma's cold, try a winter in the Wrothgarians. Bruma's a day at the beach.
We are from Bruma.

text.Jearl: The Countess sent Captain Burd to deal with that Oblivion Gate outside of town. We're all praying that they'll be all right.

text.Cirroc: If Captain Burd and the Guard can't close that Oblivion Gate, then what? Will Bruma be destroyed just like Kvatch?
The Chapel has made enemies here in the past. The Nords prefer their dragon Ysmir to our Father Akatosh.

text.Jearl: I'm sorry, but I really don't know much about the town itself.  I spend my time outdoors, walking the ridges and valleys.

text.Cirroc: We are from Bruma.

text.Jearl: We are from Bruma.

text.TarMeena: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic Argonian Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.TarMeena: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.
Too big for me. Loud. Dirty. Clowns, fools, brutes and thieves everywhere. I want to throw my gold away, I just dump it in Lake Rumare, save time.

text.GinWulm: Varnado and Maro Rufus? They don't get along. I don't understand it. I just make the armor, and keep it in good shape.

text.Wumeek: Argonians stick mostly to the river trade. We know boats and the water. We're not fussy about the sewers, either. Water cleans it all.

text.GeemJasaiin: To earn gold, Argonians must come to the city. It is a strange life, shaped stones and whiteskins everywhere.
But in the water, we are the masters, and whiteskins pay well for our skills.

text.GreyThroat: One must be very careful in the Imperial City. There are things... dangerous things... that cannot abide the light.

text.Generic Argonian Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.TarMeena: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Breton Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic Breton Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic Breton Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.HannibalTraven: Before the Arcane University was founded in the second era, Crystal Tower on Summerset Isle was the source of all magical learning.
Since then, the Imperial City has been Tamriel's foremost magical research center.

text.JulienneFanis: I rarely leave the University, as I have all I need right here. If you need ingredients, try Ogier Georick at 'The Main Ingredient.'

text.RenaldViernis: I like to walk. You can walk for hours in the city. Always something to look at, someone to talk to.

text.OgierGeorick: If I don't have what you need, try Claudette Perrick at 'The Gilded Carafe'. That's right here in the Market District.

text.EdgarVautrine: You want to buy or sell, the City is great. You want free? Go down the holes, kill some monsters. Sell your loot back in the city!

text.ClaudettePerrick: Also try my friend, Ogier Georick, The Main Ingredient, here in the District.

text.IreneMetrick: To know the right things, you have to know the right people. Ida Vlinorman, Mandil, Samuel Bantien, and Othrelos are the right people.

text.RodericPierrane: Irene Metrick and I spend a lot of time together, true. We're just good friends. But don't tell Elisa. She wouldn't understand.

text.ElisaPierrane: Roderic is looking around for a business to invest in. I know he'll find something soon.

text.KastusSintav: Whatever Uncle Iniel says. 'Lay off the Atius bastards,' he says, so we lay off.

text.BeranSintav: If we work hard, Uncle Iniel says he'll set us up in business together, maybe a little fruit orchard, or maybe tomatoes.

text.SamuelBantien: I only do the training any more. None of the rigs and tricks. Rochelle and me just want the settled life nowadays.

text.RochelleBantien: Samuel was a bit wild as a young man. The City will do that to you. Bad company, bad influences.

text.MatthiasDraconis: Master Umbacano is a fine gentleman. Mad for old Ayleid stuff, true, but he's got the dosh, so it's all right, ain't it?

text.ErnestManis: I got no beds here. You need a bed in the Imperial City, you got four choices. The King and Queens and Luther Broads are in the Gardens.
The Tiber Septim Hotel is very nice, but very expensive. There's the Bloated Float at the Waterfront. Sleep on a boat. And cheap, too.

text.JakbenImbel: It is so kind of you to favor me with your attention. Please excuse me if I seem unappreciative of the honor.
... Was I insufficiently clear? I beg your pardon. You do not interest me. We will not be having further social discourse.

text.HastrelOttus: Akatosh speaks to us all, but we never listen. Go to the Temple of the One. Read the Covenants. Praise the Nine!

text.RolandJenseric: It's not safe, talking to strangers. I don't know what's going on, but I have to be careful.

text.SalomonGeonette: Soon, the Elder Council must choose a new emperor, and then I suppose they'll sort out my commission. Until then, I just have to keep on working.

text.AncusAfranius: It's not that I'm lazy. I'm just not very ambitious. You can live comfortably in the city very cheaply. So why work yourself to death?

text.DamianMagius: We store goods here until the buyer can collect them, or until the ships come in.

text.Generic Breton Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Breton Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic DarkElf Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic DarkElf Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic DarkElf Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.BoderiFarano: Other arcane trainers in the City? Just one. Dovyn Aren. In the Market District. Basic instructor in Alteration.

text.DelosFandas: Look. It's big, see. REALLY big. Only way to learn it is to walk it. Look at everything, talk to everyone.

text.DovynAren: I was in the Thieves Guild. But I'm out now. I retired. Too old for that foolishness. I don't keep up contacts. You get out? You stay out.

text.Othrelos: The Watch can't touch me. I'm careful, private-like. Don't like people following me. Sure, it makes people nervous, seeing me sneak around. Too bad.

text.FathisUles: It is a beautiful city. I love to walk, talk with everyone, hear the news, share the little stories of the day.

text.UlenAthram: I don't miss Morrowind. All that sour Tribunal grumbling and old-fashioned ancestor worship. Good riddance.

text.DraloraAthram: Morrowind is still living in the Second Era. I can't believe how they treat Khajiit and Argonians. Here, we are Imperial citizens, nothing less.

text.SorisArenim: I don't know. Just take a walk around. Buy something. Plenty of stores. Why'd you come in the first place?

text.MyvrynaArano: People in the city, they get stuff and forget to pay. So I help 'em remember. You talk to 'em, lean on 'em a bit, and they remember right away.

text.DranasLlethro: I signed on for the Raven Rock colony. Went there as a builder. Hung around afterwards, but the money ran out.

text.Generic DarkElf Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic DarkElf Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic HighElf Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic HighElf Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic HighElf Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Palonirya: Anyone can wear clothes. But the RIGHT clothes? That is not so easy. Go to any castle. They wear Palonirya's designs, or they're nobody.

text.Calindil: No one can experience the City for you. You must go, walk, touch, see, feel, talk to everyone.

text.Atraena: The Tiber Septim Hotel is clean, comfortable, and quite exclusive. I don't mind paying a little extra for a little privacy.

text.ErissareArenim: My favorite thing is fresh slaughterfish, caught fresh from the docks on the Waterfront.

text.Umbacano: It is well known in the City that I collect Ayleid antiquities. It's true, but I desire only very specific items.

text.Areldil: I'm not in the habit of answering questions for strangers. No offense intended.

text.Seridur: I'm sorry, but my studies keep me indoors for the most part. I know little of the rest of the city.

text.Generic HighElf Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic HighElf Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Imperial Male: The daedra did a lot of damage, but we'll rebuild. Before you know it, the city will be as good as new.
Better, maybe, now that we've got the Dragon to watch over us.

text.Generic Imperial Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic Imperial Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic Imperial Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.AdamusPhillida: It is a wonderful city, and I'm proud to have served her for 40 years. But I'm ready to retire, let the young folks take over the reins.

text.HieronymusLex: Never compromise. Never blink. Never wink at injustice. Never quit trying to make this a better city for everyone.

text.ServatiusQuintilius: I aim to keep an eye on things here in the city. Take it slow, get to know the people. Try not to get off on the wrong foot.

text.AudensAvidius: When the city is quiet, everybody is happy. Right? If you like noise, maybe you're in the wrong place.

text.IrlavJarol: You know, of course, the Imperial Palace is Ayleid. White Gold Tower, they called it, back in the Middle Merethic, when the Aldmeri ruled Tamriel.
How quaint. You seek to educate yourself. At the expense of my precious time. Go. Shoo. Bother someone else.

text.MartinaFloria: I like cities, and this is the biggest and the best. All races, cultures, cuisines, crafts... the City has them all.

text.ViatorAccius: While you're in the Market District, see  Rohssan's weapons at A Fighting Chance, and see Varnado and Maro Rufus at The Best Defense for armor.

text.TertullianVerus: It's a beautiful city. But stay away from the Waterfront. It's not dangerous, but it's dirty, and the beggars are a nuisance.

text.SergiusVerus: The Black Horse Courier is run by three Khajiit brothers. They buy freelance stories with an Imperial stipend, and give the papers away for free.

text.CiceroVerus: It would be perfect... if the Watch could just get rid of the damn Thieves Guild. You don't have this problem in Anvil or Bruma.

text.MaroRufus: Well, if you MUST have Heavy Armor, see Varnado. So heavy, so ugly... but it's your choice.

text.ViniciaMelissaeia: You have complaints against merchants here? You file complaints with me. I fill out lots of forms, which go to a lot of people who ignore them.
So what else did you expect? Justice? Go to the Chapel. Talk to Zenithar. He'll take care of everything.

text.LeyMarillin: A wealthy gentleman in the Talos Plaza district named Umbacano collects Ayleid artifacts. Perhaps he has use for someone like you.

text.PistaMarillin: Where can you find a bed in the City? I hear the Tiber Septim Hotel in Talos Plaza is very nice.
In the Elven Gardens, Luther Broad's Boarding House may suit less discriminating customers.
Fighters Guild has no accommodations in town. Mages Guild members have their own quarters at the Arcane University.
I can't recommend the Bloated Float on the Waterfront. The Waterfront is not a very desirable location.

text.InielSintav: The Sintavs have always been one of the leading families in the City. We will refrain from contact with the Atius, unless provoked.

text.CyroninSintav: What Iniel says, goes. He says, lay off the Atius, I lay off the Atius. Simple.

text.CarmanaSintav: Things have been very quiet with the Atius. That suits me just fine. All this fighting is stupid. What are they fighting about? Just stupid pride.

text.LutherBroad: Daedric shrines nearby? I know of two. North of the city, south of Bruma, east of the Silver Road, is a Mephala shrine.
East of the city, at the head of the Red River, is a shrine to Vaermina.

text.IdaVlinorman: It's just a sport. Chapel climbing. The Watch doesn't like it, but you don't climb chapels while the Watch is standing around.

text.MarinusCatiotus: This city life is killing me. Work all day long. Drop dead, and they toss you in Lake Rumare. Just need to make my money at the Arena and live easy.

text.TertiusFavonius: I like the ladies. It's been my weakness. But now I've got Romana, I stay away from the fleshpots.

text.RomanaFaleria: It is SO hard to find a man you can trust in this big city. Sure, Tertius has had his share of girls. Just look at him. But all that's changed now.
The Watch is so completely on my ass. So I got to lay low for a while. I got some dosh stashed, so I'm fine for now.

text.VontanSintav: I'm a Sintav, and we Sintavs stick together. Uncle Iniel got us swell jobs and a house. It's a family thing.

text.JastiaSintav: I'm sick of all this fighting with the Atius clan. I'm glad Uncle Iniel put his foot down.

text.JenaSintav: The Sintav clan is very close. We watch out for each other, and Uncle Iniel, he knows everything, and takes care of us.

text.ItiusHayn: A short stay in our lovely Imperial Prison should cool your enthusiasm for a life of crime. The drunk tank in particular has a unique aroma.

text.AugustaCalidia: Where can you find some fun? That depends on your idea of fun. You can bet, fight, or both at the Arena.
There are plenty of sights to see, and plenty of places to shop, but the Watch frowns on brawling and adventuring in the city.

text.SevariusAtius: I agree with the Watch Captain. This Atius-Sintav feud has gone on long enough. I can control my people. I hope Iniel can control his.

text.HelvoAtius: It wasn't my fault. Cyronin Sintav started it. But I'm the one who got caught, so I'm the one who has to cool his heels.

text.LurioMaenius: If I don't find something soon, I'm going to have to try my luck at adventuring. My pals say there's a lot of caves and ruins west towards Skingrad.

text.OntusVanin: I spent 40 years at the Arcane University. Good years, but I don't miss it. Now I'm completely useless, and proud of it.

text.DynariAmnis: It's the city of Tiber Septim, youngest of the gods. Go to the Palace and the Temple of the One. Stand on the stones where Talos stood.

text.AstiniaAtius: I'm fed up with the senseless feuding, blood spilled for no good reason. Glad the Watch put a stop to it.

text.GemellusAxius: The Earl is perhaps not well known in the city. He is a private man, and keeps to himself.

text.AlessiaOttus: St. Alessia has blessed our city and all its people. Visit the Temple of the One, and renew your faith.

text.IdaOttus: Mara's blessing on you, and on all her children. Speak to her at the Temple of the One. Ask Mother Mara; she will shower your heart with love.

text.TrenusDuronius: Big city. I really LOVE the lights at night, shoo-shoo. The City of Love. Got it? Love? Light? Night? Big. Big, big, big, BIG!

text.StantusVarrid: Look around. Count the true believers. How many of these people really have faith? It's easy to have faith when everything's fine.

text.AmantiusAllectus: I'm here in the city for access to the Temple libraries, and for the bookstores... especially the First Edition in the Market District.

text.CaulaAllectus: I find things to do. I manage the house, make sure Amantius doesn't starve or run out of ink.

text.ReneeGeonette: It's so sad. Salomon was to compose a symphony for Uriel Septim, to be performed for the whole city in the Arena.

text.MaranaRian: The Temple District is by far the most desirable address in the city. Why? Because I live here, of course. Don't you agree?

text.SuriusAfranius: My housemates and I were lucky to find this house in the Temple District. It costs a little more, but it's a very good address.

text.PraxedesAfranius: It is a very fashionable address, of course, but we live simply.

text.PennusMallius: I made quite a lot of gold from my last expedition. I bought this house, invested the rest, and now I'm just living the life of the city gentleman.

text.VelanAndus: The lighthouse is mostly for show. You'd have to be an idiot to try to navigate here by night.

text.BronsilaKvinchal: I've worked on the docks as long as Vlanarus, but he thinks he's the expert. He's always looking over my shoulder, do it this way, do it that way.

text.VlanarusKvinchal: Kastav says he works. Ha! Flies land on him, he's too lazy to brush them off. I'm sick of taking abuse for him, even if he is my brother.

text.KastavKvinchal: I do my part on the docks, just like Bronsila and Vlanarus. Why should I kill myself? They don't pay me any more. For what I get paid, I work plenty.

text.RestitaStatlilia: We stable horses for folks in the Imperial City. We'd sell horses, too. Except... we can't seem to keep track of them.

text.BrielusGawey: Sure. Some folks here think horses are for riding. Then again, some of us are Orcs. Snak gra-Bura, she prefers eating stew to riding horses.

text.Generic Imperial Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Imperial Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Khajiit Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Urjabhi: The Black Horse Courier brings the news of the people to the people. We are funded by the Empire, so our broadsheets are always free!

text.Rajiradh: You see Khajiit always running through the City? You see Ra'Jiradh and his brothers! We bring the Black Horse Courier to the good citizens, yes?

text.Hassiri: We operate throughout the Imperial City and Cyrodiil. Very fast, very accurate. News happens? The Black Horse Courier is there!

text.RaJhan: Ra'jhan used to share a house, but not now. Ra'jhan is very proud, work so hard, now has house all his own.

text.Srathad: S'rathad learns the city by walking, talking, seeing it all. S'rathad thinks this is the best way for you, too.

text.Jmhad: The Arboretum. That's where J'mhad likes to go. Always quiet, always green.

text.Generic Khajiit Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Nord Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic Nord Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic Nord Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Jensine: Everyone comes to the Big City to buy and sell. Why not? More stores, better selection, better prices.

text.Agarmir: I supply many fine city merchants with goods. All sorts of things. Whatever I can buy cheap and sell dear.

text.AlgottheNortherner: I'm here because I'm a loafer. And the city's an easy place for a loafer to get by. I do odd jobs, a little adventuring, build up a little pile....

text.Generic Nord Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Nord Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Orc Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic Orc Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic Orc Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.UrbulgroOrkulg: Where else? You have to be here. This is THE City. The BIG City. Why waste time in little places?

text.DulgroShug: You just have to know the right people. Look up Ida Vlinorman and Othrelos in the Elven Gardens. They're the right people.

text.GramangroMarad: We rarely get real trouble here. The Watch puts a stop to rough stuff damn quick. I'm mostly ornamental at the Bloated Float. Makes folks happy.

text.UmoggraMarad: You'll find a lot of orcs serving as private guards. Watch work is too dull. Lots of folks say, 'Oooh, there's an orc, she's scary'. Makes it easy.

text.LuronkgroGlurzog: I'm quite behind on current events, I'm afraid. I can't be of any help to you.

text.GramangroMarad: The Bloated Float rents beds. Only place on the waterfront. Cheap. And it's safe.

text.UzulGroGrulam: Hard to find an Orc girl in this city like Umog gra-Marad. Smart, tough, got a good trade. Nice-looking, too. So I got to make my intentions clear.

text.SnakgraBura: The Chestnut Handy Stables used to sell horses. But they're gone. Our horses. All gone. Big mystery. No idea where they went. [burp]

text.Generic Orc Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Orc Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Redguard Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic Redguard Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic Redguard Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Borissean: What? There's a city out there? You don't say. What good is it, eh? Dirt. Horses. Idiots. Be my guest.

text.Delmar: Enchanting city. A real eye-full. Just walk and gawk. Stroll along the Greenway and around the Palace.

text.Phintias: This is the only book store in the city. There's also Renoit's Books in Chorrol, Mach-Na's in Cheydinhal, and Southern Books in Leyawiin.

text.Varnado: You want Light Armor? Pah! Why wear fluffy flutter, when you can wear real armor? But if you MUST have Light Armor, talk to Maro Rufus. Idiot.

text.Winson: You got to be careful. You don't want people taking notice. Just keep quiet, keep your head down.

text.Angelie: I'm content here. Some day I hope to meet the right man, but not a seaman. Never.

text.Dorian: There are many people in the city who interest me, and you are not one of them.

text.Willet: Where to sleep? The Tiber Septim Hotel in Talos Plaza is nice but expensive. Luther Broad's Boarding House in Elven Gardens is just okay.
The Bloated Float on the Waterfront is cheap... and a bit too interesting for my tastes.

text.Curtis: The Nine say each of us is special, but that's just a lie. I don't mind, but it just sounds stupid.

text.Ruslan: You're very curious. Perhaps too curious for your own good.

text.ArmandChristophe: A little tip. People who ask a lot of questions around here tend to be not very popular.

text.Jair: You have to watch out for pickpockets in the city. You'd be surprised how many waterfronters earn a good income that way.

text.IsleifTheOpenHanded: I share my good fortunes with the poor and needy. And you ain't neither. Life isn't easy on the waterfront. But we look out for each other.

text.HillodTheOutlaw: I helped build Raven Rock. Had a bad run-in with the law, so here I am. Pretty soon I'll head out for the Imperial Reserve, try my luck there.

text.Generic Redguard Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic Redguard Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic WoodElf Female: I can't get over the dragon statue in the Temple ruins. Tell me again how you and Martin defeated Mehrunes Dagon!

text.Generic WoodElf Male: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Generic WoodElf Female: Every time I walk past the Temple, I'll remember that terrible day and how you and Martin delivered us from destruction.

text.Bothiel: The orrery here is the only one in Cyrodiil. There's one more in Hammerfell... the old one at Stros M'Kai.

text.Rindir: My advice is take your time, walk around the Market District, see what's on offer. Don't buy until you've seen it all. Take your time.

text.Thoronir: I have the best prices in town? Why? I'm smart, and you're smart. We know the right people, we get the best deals.

text.Gelephor: Crime in the City? You hear a lot of complaining, but it's really not so bad. The Thieves Guild is smart; they don't want any trouble with the Watch.

text.Mandil: It pays to know about locks and lockpicks. It's just a hobby, of course, but the average citizen feels more secure when he understands his own locks.

text.Elragail: Thamriel says she hears voices. All the men and women who lived and died here for thousands of years... maybe they left ghosts behind.
I beg your pardon. The city? Here's the city. All around us. A thousand stones, a thousand souls.
I hear them all. Sometimes. But not right now. They're all quiet. Did you frighten them away?

text.Hagaer: It's terrible. I just can't walk past a bookstore. The First Edition, in the Market District, is the worst.

text.Methredhel: I think I'll do just fine. I'm a natural. Finder's keepers, right? And I'm a pretty good finder.

text.Adanrel: Lots of us on the Waterfront are down. We can't do that dungeon stuff like you adventurers. We got no money, and no skills. Nobody wants us.

text.Carwen: I'll get mine. Folks in this city got plenty of gold. Take from the rich and give to the poor, if you catch my drift.

text.Generic WoodElf Male: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.Generic WoodElf Female: We are from the IC (not to be confused with the OC).

text.UrsanneLoche: Then Aleron's death has been avenged. I told him that the gambling would lead to this, that foolish man. But he never listened.
Before you go, I have this for you. Aleron told me that if he ever got in trouble, this could be used to bail him out of jail.
He'll... not be needing it any longer, and I want you to have it. I'll not take no for an answer.
I know you did all you could, and for that, I thank you. Now, please... go in peace. I wish to be alone.
When I saw the grave look on your face, I knew something had happened to him. And what of that fetcher, Kurdan?

text.AleronLoche: Don't bother. The door to this place is now locked. The only way to get out is by decending into the Hunter's Run and killing the Hunters.
One of them will have the key to the door. That's Kurdan's rules. It's the only way we can win.
I wish I could help more, but I can't fight. I've never held a weapon before in my life. Please... get us out of here!
I'm not a rich man, but if we get out of here alive, I'll do what I can to reward you.
Kurdan doesn't make most of his money being a simple usurer. He also invented what he calls the Hunter's Run.
People pay him a great deal of money to hunt and kill living human prey. No questions asked, and he takes care of the bodies.
He uses the dungeons under Fort Grief as the hunting grounds. I was placed here because he knew someone would go looking for me.
I'm sorry you got mixed up in all of this. I hope you can fight. It's our only chance of escaping alive.

text.Generic Argonian Female: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.MachNa: Imperials hate Dark Elves; Dark Elves hate Imperials. Imperials hate that a no-name Hlaalu trader got made into a count.
Andel Indarys doesn't help his case by having a prat for a son, and a wife that dies in very suspicious circumstances.
Our Dark Elves left Morrowind to get away from the Church and State, and they don't like it when Imperials get all holy and patriotic with them.
Of course, local Dark Elves tend to be money-grubbing, alcoholic low-brows with little education or culture.
Since I read a lot, and speak well, and don't drink brandy from milk pails, I guess I qualify as an Imperial.
But on the whole, I like Cheydinhal's Dark Elves better than I like the Imperials, so go figure....

text.Deetsan: It's all right. The Guild here, that is. That's what you meant, right? It's fine. I'm doing fine here.

text.Generic Argonian Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.UlrichLeland: Count Indarys has ordered us to hold our positions until Farwil returns from inside that accursed Oblivion Gate.

text.Generic Breton Male: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.

text.Generic Breton Female: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.Generic Breton Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Breton Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.AndelIndarys: I can only hope that Farwil and his knights manage to close that Oblivion Gate. The fate of Cheydinhal hangs in the balance!

text.Generic DarkElf Male: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.

text.Generic DarkElf Female: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.TovasSelvani: I could tell you our blacks are the fastest, toughest, most reliable horses in Cyrodiil.

text.MivrynaArano: Tovas knows his horses, and I'll stay with him and these beautiful creatures. Forever.

text.DerveraRomalen: Here you have your Chapel-going Imperials, and your Chapel-dodging Dark Elves, and never shall the twain meet.
The Imperials have the gold, houses, and top spots. Dark Elves like me left Morrowind and the whole priest-ridden Tribunal nightmare...
... and we take the whole patriotic 'Imperial Mission' attitude with a dose of salt.

text.AndelIndarys: Just look around. Is not Cheydinhal the model of civic rule? No... don't bow! I am just a humble servant of the people.

text.UleneHlervu: You worship the Nine Divines, perhaps? Have they ever helped or harmed you? Of course not.
Now, worship a Daedra Lord, and you get effects... bad ones, of course, but clear and measurable effects.

text.TolisiGirith: He pays peanuts. And thinks it entitles him to chew us out 18 hours a day? Sometimes I wonder if I made a mistake coming here.

text.TanasaArano: Lots of us Dark Elves came to Cyrodiil to get away from the Temple. We're sick of living under the thumb of the priests, and scraping by on the dole.

text.Generic DarkElf Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic DarkElf Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic HighElf Male: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.

text.Generic HighElf Female: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.Ohtesse: I'm happy to be of service in any way I can, in any place I can. There are so many who need help, and so few to offer it.

text.Errandil: It's a scandal that the Mages Guild has tolerated practice of the Black Arts among its members for so long.
The current Arch-Mage, Hannibal Traven, is true and bold to prohibit necromancy, reversing the Guild's shameful past policies of official tolerance.

text.Ohtimbar: I worked the Arena in the Imperial City for a while. Got up to Gladiator, then took a powder. A guy could get hurt, you know.

text.Falcar: I am the chapter head of the Cheydinhal Mages Guild. It is quite an honor... but they had no choice, since I'm the only semi-competent one here.

text.Orintur: I'm very fond of Cheydinhal. It's where I met my love, Eilonwy. Our lives are quite long, and choosing the right partner is very important.

text.Eilonwy: Perhaps it seems silly, but our love is the most important thing in all creation. Orintur and I spend all our time together, in the High Elf way.

text.Voranil: You're not on my list. And that's all I have to say. If you were somebody, I'd know. But I don't, so you aren't.

text.Generic HighElf Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic HighElf Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Imperial Male: Count Indarys has ordered us to hold our positions until Farwil returns from inside that accursed Oblivion Gate.

text.MQ11CheydinhalSoldier01: Count Indarys has ordered us to hold our positions until Farwil returns from inside that accursed Oblivion Gate.

text.Generic Imperial Male: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.

text.Generic Imperial Female: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.MarianaAncharia: The Count, Andel Indarys, is a Hlaalu parvenu, but his steward, Naspia Cosma, does her best to coach him on the finer points of Imperial etiquette.
Our most celebrated citizen is Rythe Lythandas, the famous painter. Speak to his wife, and she might let you take a peek into his studio.

text.TertiaViducia: Did you know we have the finest horses in Cyrodiil, right here in town? Black Waterside Stables... the best thoroughbred blacks.

text.GruiandGarrana: I closely supervise the priests and healers of Cheydinhal Chapel, so they might more closely approach the sacred ideals of our faith.

text.NaspiaCosma: To be frank, I'd prefer a career in the Arena to this paper-pusher's position.

text.Generic Imperial Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Imperial Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Raqanar: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.
Ra'qanar is your friend, no? Your servant? Whatever you require? Ra'qanar knows nothing... less, even. But Ra'qanar wishes to please.
We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Nord Male: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.

text.HiltheTall: I came here because I love nature. And because I didn't want to serve as a boot wizard in a mountain legion in Skyrim.

text.KeldoftheIsles: I've settled down here. Nice place. A little slow, but it suits me. Burz gro-Khash is a bear sometimes, but I got thick skin. Doesn't bother me.

text.Generic Nord Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Orc Male: Business is bad with that damn Oblivion Gate outside of town. You think things can't get any worse, and then they do.

text.Generic Orc Female: Business is bad with that damn Oblivion Gate outside of town. You think things can't get any worse, and then they do.

text.BorbagraUzgash: I'm retired from adventuring... but you might try the old mine they call 'Rickety Mine' out east along the Blue Road.
Another possibility in that direction might be Kemen. It's an old Ayleid ruin.
You might also look at Quickwater Cave to the north. I cleared it out, but I haven't been there in years. It might have new tenants.

text.MagubgraOrum: Treasure holes near Cheydinhal?  Not close by.
Fort Naso and Fort Facian, though... bad news. Undead, and then some. But far out and foul enough, you'll get plenty of action.

text.BurzGroKhash: The Guild is going to hell in a hogcart. Look at what they give me? Keld of the Isles? Ohtimbar? Both Guardian rank? Phah! Useless.

text.DulfishgroOrum: Look. A fly. Buzz, buzz. Hey. Look everybody! I'm talking to a fly! Buzz, buzz, buzz!

text.MagubgraOrum: You stupid or something? What are you doing here? Go back where you came from. We don't like your kind here.

text.RogmeshgraCoblug: Voranil got parties near about every night, and there's plenty of cooking and cleaning and preparing to be done. If you don't mind.

text.MaknokgroCoblug: It's a grand house, Riverside, and they have grand parties there. All the rich swongs and swells of the town come in. Leave a right mess, they do.

text.OghashgraMagul: What are you asking me for? Do I look like Vile's dog or something? Go on. Knit a doily or play a flute or something.

text.BazurgroGharz: Boss uglies in Cheydinhal are the Orums. Don't mean nothing to you. You is the Outside. Just stay Outside, and everything's Mister Tinker. Got me?

text.Generic Orc Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Orc Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Redguard Male: The whole town is on edge with that Oblivion Gate open just outside the walls.

text.Shelley: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.TrayvondtheRedguard: My progress through the ranks here will be slow. My prejudices against certain types of magic limit my chances for advancement.

text.Generic Redguard Male: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Shelley: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic WoodElf Female: Everyone is waiting to see if Farwil and his knights return from inside that dreadful Oblivion Gate. Such brave lads!

text.Uurwen: Well, to be honest, I don't think we have much of a team in the Cheydinhal guildhall. We lack leadership, and individually, we aren't very skilled.

text.Ganredhel: You got your people, and you got your dogs. Dogs are loyal and stupid. People are smart and devious. I'll stick with dogs.

text.Generic WoodElf Female: We are from Cheydinhal.

text.Generic Argonian Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic Argonian Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.Marz: I came to Bravil because Mara called me. Bravil is not my home. I miss Black Marsh. But I shall serve here, so long as Mara needs me.

text.KudEi: I take my duties as chapter head very seriously... unlike SOME guild mages. It infuriates me how casual some guild heads are about common civility.

text.CitySwimmer: Ha! Members of the Thieves Guild in our fair town? What makes you think that? Never! Absurd! Such fine law-abiding citizens are we all!
What? You have not eyes to see? The castle, of course! The only challenge worthy of a swift sneaker.

text.Generic Argonian Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Argonian Female: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Breton Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic Breton Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.IsabeauBienne: You MUST have a fast horse! Travel quickly to ruined forts and caves nearby! It will pay for itself in precious time saved!

text.AntoineBranck: The Count was once a tournament champion. Now he's a loafer and skirt-chaser. And his son, Gellius, is a spoiled good-for-nothing skooma-sucker.

text.ChanaMona: Uravasa and Marz leave me little to do here in Bravil. That leaves me free to devote my time to Mara's ministry throughout the Empire.

text.DelphineJend: I love my work. Fire, frost, shock, poison... little presents for Kynareth's cute little woodland creatures.

text.LucianaGalena: Other Bravil trainers? City-Swimmer teaches Sneak. Dro'shanji teaches Security. Varon Vamori teaches Speechcraft.

text.RoxanneBrigette: Me? I got no problem with Bravil. Lovely town. That little prince, the count's boy, he's sweet with the sugar. EEEA-sy Street, all the way.

text.Generic Breton Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Breton Female: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic DarkElf Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic DarkElf Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.UravasaOthrelas: Mara guides and protects Bravil, like she protects any good family. Like any good family, we have our problems.

text.FathisAren: Far be it from me to criticize my patron and sovereign. Bravil obviously flourishes under his wise and beneficent rule.

text.DrelsTheran: The Renrijra Krin are Khajiit bandits and smugglers posing as guerillas and freedom fighters.

text.TadroseHelas: There's a lot of adventuring action from here south to Blackwood, and everyone comes to me with their gear.

text.VaronVamori: Old, worn, and wicked. Wet, wounded, and wild. Empty as the eastern horizon, dusk on the Niben. Solemn and bitter as the grave.

text.Generic DarkElf Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic DarkElf Female: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic HighElf Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic HighElf Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.Gilgondorin: My neighbor, Dro'shanji, is worried. He's seen creatures around the house lately. Why don't you talk to Dro'shanji, see if you can help?
Have you looked around? Bravil is Tamriel's cloaca. Silverhome is the only decent place in town. Don't know why I stay here.

text.Ungarion: There are two ruined forts south of Bravil. One is close to the road to Leyawiin. The other is out on a point of land that projects into Niben Bay.

text.Ardaline: I'm afraid I'm not very social. So I really don't know very much about the people here.

text.Aryarie: Bravil? Good points? Cheap to live. Unpretentious. Free-wheeling. Bad points? Culturally, a hole. Count's a clown and his son's a skooma-sucker.

text.Carandial: The Ayelid ruin of Anutwyll is nearby. I can spend a few days on site, then return here for the comforts of home and my library.

text.Ranaline: Excuse me. I stay to myself. I have always found the wrong sort of friends. Now I do without.

text.Generic HighElf Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic HighElf Female: We are from Bravil.

text.RegulusTerentius: I won't risk my Guard attacking that infernal Oblivion Gate. We'll hold the walls and hope for the best.

text.Generic Imperial Male: The Count put the Guard on high alert. We'll be ready if the daedra decide to attack, don't worry.

text.VieraLerus: The Count put the Guard on high alert. We'll be ready if the daedra decide to attack, don't worry.

text.Generic Imperial Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic Imperial Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.RegulusTerentius: Yes, yes, Count of Bravil. Are you a foreigner? Do yourself a favor. Learn the basics about the places you visit. There. Problem solved.

text.GelliusTerentius: Yes. Bravil. How clever of you. You've already learned the name of the town and county. I see a great future for you in public service.

text.VieraLerus: The Count used to be a great man, but power and idleness have spoilt him. However, we remain loyal in memory of past kindnesses, and to serve Bravil.

text.ItaRienus: Bravil is an important trade center, and a rich melting pot of Imperial, Khajiit, and Argonian cultures. And, yes, a bit shabby and shopworn.

text.Generic Imperial Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Imperial Female: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Khajiit Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic Khajiit Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.DroNahrah: The Count is too preoccupied with his pastimes to spend time on county affairs. So the burden lies on me.

text.Nahsi: The Fighters Guild is good enough to encourage me in sharing the inner peace and spiritual harmony of the martial arts.

text.Droshanji: Bravil is perhaps not so nice. But Bravil Castle, and castle gardens, they are jewels, are they not?

text.Skrivva: Well, perhaps, yes, one hears such things, what is one to believe? That S'krivva collects goods of untestable provenance? Pshaw. Rumors.
Bravil perhaps presents little scope for an ambitious member of our guild. Perhaps you may find the castle entertaining. Little else.

text.JzinDar: You are stupid, so I'll make myself clear... you are stupid. Go away. I don't want your blood and puke all over me.

text.Rvanni: R'vanni just wants to get along. No trouble. Anything you want. R'vanni's know-nothing, good-for-nothing. Ask anyone. Just don't hurt R'vanni.

text.Generic Khajiit Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Khajiit Female: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Nord Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic Nord Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.OlavatheFair: My task is to know and love the people of Bravil as if they were my own children. If you have ever been a parent, you know what a challenge that is.

text.HansBlackNail: I was with the Count when he was young, and a shining star on the tournament path. I only wish he'd straighten his son out.

text.ReistrtheRotted: Been here. Right here! All day! Last night, too! I wasn't there! Not there at all! I can totally prove it! Ask anyone!

text.Generic Nord Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Nord Female: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic Orc Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.BogrumGroGalash: A local woman, Ursanne Loche, has a missing husband. She might appreciate some help from someone like you.

text.BrokilgroShatur: It is a terrible responsibility, being Bravil's First Citizen of the Ale Tub, but I suffer under the burden like a Sure-Green Orc.

text.Generic Orc Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic WoodElf Male: We're all wondering when more of those evil Gates are going to open. I'd leave town if I dared.

text.Generic WoodElf Female: Didn't you see that Oblivion Gate just outside the walls? Mara preserve us from the fate of Kvatch!

text.Nilawen: What's a pretty young thing like me doing in this swamp town? I inherited the business from my late husband, and I aim to make it work.

text.Daenlin: I have nothing to say about the Count and his son. The rest of the town is a little rough. But I don't mind. I like it that way.

text.Generic WoodElf Male: We are from Bravil.

text.Generic WoodElf Female: We are from Bravil.

text.KurdangroDragol: Do you really think I could afford to let you leave here? The key you found is a fake. No prey has ever left this island alive.
And I aim to keep it that way. You were right about one thing though...
This IS my game, and I'm changin' the rules!

text.Generic Nord Male: Suit yourself. I'm sure it isn't anything important.
Ah, it's coming back to me now. Yeah, seems I saw someone looking out the window at Jearl's house the other day.
Someone I'd never seen before. When Jearl wasn't home. You see what I mean?
Now, if you'll excuse me, all this talk has given me a powerful thirst. Thankee kindly.

text.Regner: She's just back from a trip south, they say. Haven't seen hide nor hair of her myself though. Stays indoors all day long, I guess.

text.RightWind: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Generic Breton Male: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Generic Breton Female: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.AlvalUvani: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Generic HighElf Male: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Karinnarre: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.ArnoraAuria: Not that it's anybody's business, but I have noticed voices coming from Jearl's house. But I've never seen anybody but Jearl go in or out. Strange.

text.Generic Imperial Male: Not on my watch. Captain Burd will know for sure, though. We all report to him.
Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Generic Imperial Female: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Jskar: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.OngartheWorldWeary: Well, since I like you ... I think there's somebody staying with Jearl.
Never seen 'em, but I've heard her talking to someone, and I've seen somebody at the window when Jearl wasn't home.
None of my business, but since you asked ...

text.Generic Nord Male: Nothing comes to mind. Of course, my memory sometimes ain't what it used to be.
Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Generic Nord Female: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.BumphgraGash: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Cirroc: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Jearl: Not that I can think of. People are mostly staying home, what with all the troubles in the world.

text.Burd: Really? That is odd. I know for certain that she returned alone. I don't like it.
Since you're working with Cloud Ruler Temple, I'm going to authorize you to search Jearl's house. I'll pass the word to my men. We won't interfere.

text.Jauffre: Excellent work. I knew I could count on you. The gods did not idly choose you as their agent, whatever you may think.
But we have not eliminated the threat against Bruma and Cloud Ruler Temple, only delayed it. I will warn the Countess of the danger.
You should speak to Martin. I believe he has made some progress with the Mysterium Xarxes.
This makes for grim reading. The Mythic Dawn did not take long to locate Martin again.
The document speaks of two agents. You need to eliminate both of them.
Excellent work. I knew I could count on you. The gods did not idly choose you as their agent, whatever you may think.
But it is clear that Mankar Camoran will soon bring all his power to bear against Bruma. I will warn the Countess of the danger.
You should speak to Martin. I believe he has made some progress with the Mysterium Xarxes.
Good. But there may still be more spies out there. You should continue to search for their base of operations in Bruma.
Very well. Keep looking. We must uncover those spies and find out what they know.
You must eliminate both the Mythic Dawn agents in Bruma. We cannot allow them to continue to plot against us.
Thank you. Talk to Steffan. He can tell you where he has seen them.
Captain Burd in Bruma may also be able to help. I've asked the Countess to have the guard keep an eye out for strangers.
Track down the spies and kill them. Find out what they know, and what they're plannning, if possible.
Ah, yes. I hope you can help. The gate guards have reported seeing strangers on the road for the past several nights.
I cannot leave Cloud Ruler undefended while my men search the whole mountainside, but these spies must be eliminated.

text.Steffan: We always see them near the runestone at dusk. They aren't too woodcrafty, but Grandmaster Jauffre has forbidden us to range too far from the walls.
But it seems that you have been given the freedom to attack the enemy that we all crave! Good luck. We will keep the Emperor safe here, don't worry.

text.Burd: Except for Jearl coming back from a trip down south, things are pretty quiet. Not much travel right now with the Oblivion Crisis.
I've told my men to keep a sharp eye out, but I've had no reports of any strangers in town.
What about you? Turned up anything suspicious?
Nothing new to report on my end. Have you uncovered anything suspicious?
I trust that you'll handle things ... appropriately. The less I know about it, the better.

text.SESheogorath: I do. I did. And I won't say it again. But, that's enough about that. You're the ruler of Dementia! Just look at you. You're positively beaming!
You now have the power to summon Dark Seducers. They've always served the Duke of Dementia. I think they have a thing for pain.
And here is the Ring of Lordship, a symbol of your new station. Symbols are important. They carry weight in this Realm, and others.
You would be well served to remember that.
No! Let him go!
Then go, Thadon. Have your Greenmote. Take a bath. But leave. Before I decorate my throne with your insides.
Change will preserve us! It is the lifeblood of the Isles. It will move mountains! It will mount movements!
Fool? Visionary! Change is in the air, Thadon. Breathe it deep! Bathe in its scent! Bottle it up. Save some for later.
Calm yourself, Thadon. You're making my teeth itch. You still hold your office. I suggest you see to your duties.
Hold your tongue, little Duke, or I'll tear it from your mouth.

text.SEThadon: Enough! I go to Jyggalag. I give myself to him, as a Priest of Order! This isn't done, Madgod. I think it's just started.
Yes. That's it. I'll go. Away. Far away. Working for them is like working for us, but without all the dying.
No. No. Certainly not. This isn't good. I'm sure it's bad. I can't do this anymore. No more.
Order approaches! It's taken the Fringe already! With Order clothes and Order hats! And you speak of "change"?
Ridiculous! You can't do this! Although... you're omnipotent. Or just tall. It's one of the two, I'm sure. And a fool!
But, this... stranger? Someone new? From somewhere else? Not here. I'm sure of that. I don't understand. Or I can't.
Syl... my... Syl is dead? This can't be right. Is this right? What have you done? Have you done this?

text.Ocheeva: Lucien isn't here very often. His duties with the Black Hand keep him very busy, so he trusts me to keep the Sanctuary in order.

text.Teinaava: Ocheeva and I have known Lucien since we were hatchlings. He is the one who trained us in the way of the Shadowscale, and is like a father to us.

text.MathieuBellamont: You should take some time to admire his corpse. It really is a thing of beauty. The punctures and slashes are almost... poetic.

text.VicenteValtieri: When I first joined the family, this Sanctuary was controlled by another Speaker. Lucien took over when she was killed while fulfilling a contract.

text.AntoinettaMarie: I will always think of Lucien Lachance as my savior. When he found me, I was living in a gutter, an inch away from death. I owe him everything.

text.BanusAlor: The four of us attacking him in unison was as graceful and beautiful as a ballet! The flashing of steel, the spraying of blood!

text.Arquen: When we confronted Lachance he tried to defend himself, tried to declare his innocence! But we would not hear his treacherous lies!
As you can see, he was no match for the combined power of the Black Hand, even weakened as we are.
I... I don't even know what to say. How could we have been so wrong? Lucien tried to explain, but we wouldn't listen...
But he is certainly in a better place now. Lucien Lachance's soul now serves Sithis in the Void. It is an honor he earned, and deserves.

text.BelisariusArius: Most of my time is now spent on administrative duties. I have not had blood on my hands in far too long! Killing Lachance was pure ecstacy.

text.GogrongroBolmog: I once saw Lucien deal with an insubordinate Brother, someone who had broken the Tenets. It took me a week to get the blood off my boots.

text.Telaendril: Actually, Lucien did not try to recruit me. Not at first. He tried to kill me. My father wanted me dead, and he hired the Dark Brotherhood to do it.
I escaped from Lucien, and paid my father back for his treachery. Lucien came to me again that night with an offer I just couldn't refuse.

text.VicenteValtieri: The Dark Brotherhood is not in the business of staging deaths, no matter how much gold is offered. Sithis demands blood, and blood must be paid.
In order to accept the contract, we demanded a life. Motierre offered his mother, and we accepted. Lucien has already taken care of that... detail.

text.Teekeeus: I suggest you deliver that book as soon as possible. Your recommendation depends on it.
No? Are you quite sure? I would hate to think that you do, in fact, have the book, and simply have no intention of turning it over.
Very well. Should you happen to find it, it would be in the best interest of all for it to be secure here within the guild hall.
I see. Perhaps it's just as well. The book is best left in secret.
If you were to know of its whereabouts, I trust that you would bring it to me immediately.

text.Earana: Then why are we speaking? We have nothing to discuss unless you bring me that book. Now go away.
Then why are we speaking? We have nothing to discuss unless you bring me that book. Now go away.

text.Teekeeus: Finally. I shall see to it that the book is kept safe until the Council decides what should be done with it.
I shall also overlook your... transgression, and send a recommendation to the Arcane University.
Is this an attempt at humor? If so, I am not amused. Produce that book immediately.
Ah, yes. This is indeed the correct book. You've not been able to open it, I presume? Then all is well.
You have shown yourself worthy of the guild, and for that I thank you. You shall have the recommendation you need.
Now, I must ensure this book is kept safe. Excuse me.
Ah, yes. This is indeed the correct book. You've not been able to open it, I presume? Then all is well.
You have helped ensure that this book will remain safe from those who would misuse it. You have the Guild's thanks. Now, if you'll excuse me...
This is not a matter for levity. If you have truly found the book, I expect you to bring it here once you have possession of it.

text.Earana: Ah, wonderful! I'll just take this from you, and get to work translating it. I'll need some time with this; come and find me tomorrow.
I'll be here until I've finished my work. But please don't disturb me until I'm done; this is quite a delicate business, you see.
Ah, wonderful! I'll just take this from you, and get to work translating it. I'll need some time with this; come and find me tomorrow.
